explanation: Encodes 'is f(n) = o(n) for almost all n?' as the existence of a density-1 set A along which f(n) = o(n), and negates it. The junk value f(n) = 0 at unrepresented n could only make this weaker if the unrepresented n had density 1. The page notes f is likely defined for all n ≥ 6, and almost all odd n are known to be represented, so the negation correctly reflects Tao's density bound.
